In Australia and some other parts of the commonwealth our profession is separated into barristers/solicitors. Barristers usually start out as solicitors before going to the bar which involves some further training in advocacy and courtroom skills.

Barristers have to take any case offered to them unless it's outside their field of experience. They cannot be engaged by a member of the public and can only be engaged by a solicitor to appear on behalf of their clients. They cannot be employees or operate in partnership with others so they stay independent. They do exclusively advice and trial work, no transactional law.
